question: Which statement best describes Main idea?
options: A commit saves a set of changes with a message explaining their purpose. It is like a labeled checkpoint you can return to or compare later. Keep commits focused so reviewers can understand them. Before committing, inspect the changed files and make sure generated secrets or unrelated edits are not included. For example, commit a focused change with a message that says what the edit accomplishes.

A branch is a named line of work based on a previous commit. You can change files on a branch without changing the main branch. It is like making a copy of a draft for an experiment. Branches make parallel work easier, but they do not automatically prevent conflicts when two changes edit the same lines. For example, create a branch for a task so unfinished work does not alter the shared main branch.

A repository is a folder whose file history is tracked by Git. It includes the project files and the record of changes. It is like a notebook that keeps earlier drafts, not just the latest page. A repository may live on your computer and on a hosting service such as GitHub. For example, clone the repository to make a local working copy before editing a feature.

A merge combines changes from one branch into another. Git may do this automatically, or it may ask you to resolve a conflict when both branches changed the same area. It is like combining two edited pages and choosing what to keep where they disagree. Run the project checks after resolving conflicts. For example, resolve a merge conflict by comparing both intended changes, not by choosing a side blindly.
explanation: A repository is a folder whose file history is tracked by Git. It includes the project files and the record of changes. It is like a notebook that keeps earlier drafts, not just the latest page. A repository may live on your computer and on a hosting service such as GitHub. For example, clone the repository to make a local working copy before editing a feature.
